# Manage SCIM Tokens

This topic describes how to generate, rotate, and delete SCIM tokens in <!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name -->Terraform Enterprise<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name --><!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:product-name -->HCP Terraform<!-- END: TFC:only name:product-name -->. Your identity provider (IdP) uses SCIM tokens to authenticate with <!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name -->Terraform Enterprise<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name --><!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:product-name -->HCP Terraform<!-- END: TFC:only name:product-name --> when provisioning users and groups.

## Overview

SCIM tokens are bearer tokens that authenticate your identity provider when it communicates with <!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name -->Terraform Enterprise's<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name --><!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:product-name -->HCP Terraform's<!-- END: TFC:only name:product-name --> SCIM endpoints. The IdP includes the token in the `Authorization` header of each SCIM API request.

SCIM tokens have the following characteristics:

- Tokens are valid only for `/scim/v2/*` endpoints. They cannot access other <!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name -->Terraform Enterprise<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name --><!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:product-name -->HCP Terraform<!-- END: TFC:only name:product-name --> APIs.
<!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:token-expiration -->
- Tokens created through the API default to 365 days when no expiration is specified. You can configure token expiration up to 12 months.
<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:token-expiration -->

<!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:token-expiration -->
- Tokens have a mandatory expiration date that you must set at creation. You can set the expiration between 30 days and one year from the creation date.
<!-- END: TFC:only name:token-expiration -->

<!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:multiple-tokens -->
-  You can create multiple active tokens simultaneously. This enables zero-downtime token rotation. Refer to the [Public SCIM API](/terraform/enterprise/api-docs/scim) for public SCIM rate-limit behavior.
<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:multiple-tokens -->

<!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:multiple-tokens -->
- Only one active token is supported at a time. Rotation involves a brief window where SCIM synchronization may be interrupted. Refer to [Rotate a token](#rotate-a-token) for guidance on minimizing interruption.
<!-- END: TFC:only name:multiple-tokens -->

### Token properties

Each SCIM token has the following properties:

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Description | A human-readable label to help identify the token's purpose. |
| Token value | The secret bearer token value. <!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:token-storage -->Terraform Enterprise stores tokens as one-way hashes using HMAC-SHA512, so the original value cannot be retrieved. Terraform Enterprise only displays this value once at creation time.<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:token-storage --><!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:token-storage -->The token value is displayed only once at creation time and cannot be retrieved afterward.<!-- END: TFC:only name:token-storage --> |
| Created at | The timestamp when the token was created. |
| Expired at | The timestamp when the token expires. <!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:expiry-default -->Tokens created through the API default to 365 days if no expiration is specified.<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:expiry-default --><!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:expiry-default -->Expiration is mandatory and must be set between 30 days and one year at creation time.<!-- END: TFC:only name:expiry-default --> |
| Last used at | The timestamp when the token was last used for a SCIM API request. Updated with a 1-minute throttle to reduce database writes. |

## Requirements

<!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:requirements -->
Only site administrators can create, view, and revoke SCIM tokens. For more information about site admin permissions, refer to [Site Administration Permissions](/terraform/enterprise/users-teams-organizations/users#site-admin-permissions).

Before using SCIM tokens for provisioning, enable SCIM. Terraform Enterprise only accepts SCIM token-authenticated provisioning requests while SCIM is enabled. Refer to [Configure SCIM provisioning](/terraform/enterprise/scim/configure) for instructions.
<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:requirements -->

<!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:requirements -->
Only members of the [owners team](/terraform/cloud-docs/users-teams-organizations/permissions/organization#organization-owners) can create, view, and revoke SCIM tokens.

Before using SCIM tokens for provisioning, enable SCIM. Refer to [Configure SCIM provisioning](/terraform/cloud-docs/scim/configure) for instructions.
<!-- END: TFC:only name:requirements -->

## Create a SCIM token

<!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:create-token -->
To create a new SCIM token:

1. Open your user icon menu and click **Site Admin**.
2. Click **SCIM** in the left navigation.
3. In the **SCIM Tokens** section, click **Create Token**.
4. Enter a **Description** for the token, for example `IdP name` or `environment`.
5. Optionally, set the token expiration. You can choose one of the following presets: **30-day**, **90-day**, or **365-day**.
6. Click **Create Token**.
7. Copy the token value and store it securely. You will not be able to retrieve it again.

Terraform Enterprise stores tokens as one-way hashes using HMAC-SHA512. As a result, the original token value cannot be retrieved after creation. If you lose the token, you must create a new one.

After creating the token, configure your identity provider to use this token for SCIM provisioning. Refer to the IdP-specific configuration guides:

- [Configure Okta for SCIM](/terraform/enterprise/scim/configure/okta)
- [Configure Microsoft Entra ID for SCIM](/terraform/enterprise/scim/configure/entra-id)

Note that Terraform Enterprise blocks SCIM token creation while you are impersonating another user. Refer to [Impersonating a User](/terraform/enterprise/application-administration/resources#impersonating-a-user) for more information.
<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:create-token -->

<!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:create-token -->
Token creation is part of the initial SCIM setup flow in HCP Terraform. Refer to the [Enable SCIM](/terraform/cloud-docs/scim/configure#enable-scim) section of the configure guide for instructions. To replace an expired or lost token, refer to [Rotate a token](#rotate-a-token).
<!-- END: TFC:only name:create-token -->

## List tokens

<!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:list-tokens -->
You can view all SCIM tokens from the SCIM settings page:

1. Open your user icon menu and click **Site Admin**.
1. Click **SCIM** in the left navigation.
1. View the list of tokens in the **SCIM Tokens** section.

The token list displays metadata for each token, including the description, creation date, expiration date, and last used timestamp. The list does not display the secret token values.
<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:list-tokens -->

<!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:list-tokens -->
You can view existing active SCIM tokens on the **SCIM provisioning** page. You can access the page from your organization settings. 
<!-- END: TFC:only name:list-tokens -->

Use the **Last used** timestamp to identify which tokens are actively in use by your identity provider. <!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name -->Terraform Enterprise<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name --><!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:product-name -->HCP Terraform<!-- END: TFC:only name:product-name --> updates this value with a 1-minute throttle, so recent requests may not appear immediately.

## Delete a token

Deleting a SCIM token revokes access. Revoking a token immediately invalidates it, and any SCIM requests using that token fail with an HTTP `401 Unauthorized` error. You can delete a token at any time.

<Warning>

Revoking a token is immediate and irreversible. If your identity provider is actively using the token, SCIM requests authenticated with that token begin failing until you update the IdP with a new token.

</Warning>

To delete a token:

<!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:delete-token -->
1. Open your user icon menu and click **Site Admin**.
1. Click **SCIM** in the left navigation.
1. In the **SCIM Tokens** section, locate the token you want to delete.
1. Click the delete icon next to the token.
1. Confirm the deletion.
<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:delete-token -->

<!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:delete-token -->
1. Navigate to your organization settings, then click **SCIM provisioning**
1. In the row containing the token you want to delete, click the trash icon in the **Actions** column of the tokens table.
1. When prompted, enter `delete` in the dialog, then click **Delete** to continue. 
<!-- END: TFC:only name:delete-token -->

## Rotate a token

<!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:rotate-token -->
To rotate a SCIM token with zero downtime:

1. Generate a new token before the old token expires. Refer to [Token properties](#token-properties) for expiration details.
1. Update your identity provider with the new token value.
1. Verify the new token works by checking that SCIM provisioning operations succeed and the new token's **Last used at** timestamp updates.
1. Delete the old token after confirming the new token is working.

Terraform Enterprise supports multiple active tokens, so you can rotate tokens without interrupting SCIM provisioning.
<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:rotate-token -->

<!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:rotate-token -->
To rotate a SCIM token:

1. Generate a new token by following the steps in [Enable SCIM](/terraform/cloud-docs/scim/configure#enable-scim). Set a new expiration date between 30 days and one year.
1. Update your identity provider** with the new token value immediately. SCIM synchronization fails until the IdP uses a valid token.
1. Verify the new token works by checking that SCIM provisioning operations succeed.

Because only one active token is supported at a time, there is a brief window between generating the new token and updating your IdP during which SCIM synchronization may fail. Rotate tokens proactively before expiration to minimize the impact of this window.

If a token has already expired or been lost, refer to the recovery steps in [Troubleshoot SCIM provisioning](/terraform/cloud-docs/scim/troubleshooting#401-unauthorized-errors).
<!-- END: TFC:only name:rotate-token -->

## Expired token status

<!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:expired-token -->
Terraform Enterprise does not send alerts before a SCIM token expires. When a token has expired, Terraform Enterprise surfaces that status in the following places:

- On the **Site Admin** > **SCIM** page, a page alert appears above the SCIM settings.
- In the **Site Admin** navigation, a warning icon appears next to **SCIM provisioning**.

The token list shows an expiration badge for each token, including whether it is expired or when it will expire.
<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:expired-token -->

<!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:expired-token -->
No alerts are sent before a SCIM token expires. The expiration status for each token is visible on the **SCIM provisioning**.

When an expired token causes `401 Unauthorized` errors, refer to [Troubleshoot SCIM provisioning](/terraform/cloud-docs/scim/troubleshooting#401-unauthorized-errors) for recovery steps.
<!-- END: TFC:only name:expired-token -->

Rotate tokens before they expire to avoid downtime.

## Best practices for managing tokens

- Use descriptive names for tokens, such as IdP name, environment, and creation date.
- Plan for rotation and set reminders before expiration.

<!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:expiration-reminder -->
- Set a calendar reminder one to two weeks before your token expires. Tokens have a mandatory expiration of 30 days to one year and no expiration alerts are sent.
<!-- END: TFC:only name:expiration-reminder -->

- Monitor token usage and remove unused tokens.
- Limit token lifetime according to your security policy.
- Store token values securely and never share them through insecure channels.
